title: Same Count, Every Channel
subtitle: Norovirus Thresholds, Reporting & Turnaround

brief.userPrompt: Thursday, February 18, 2027 (all times Central ship time). MV Halcyon Dawn, Captain Anneliese Moreau, sails from Cozumel at 18:00 on the seven-night western Caribbean voyage that left Galveston on February 14 with 2,980 passengers and 1,120 crew and is due back in Galveston at 07:00 on Sunday, February 21. At 18:00 the signed medical log, signed by Chief Medical Officer Dr. Fiona Gallagher, shows 41 passenger cases (1.4 percent) and 9 crew cases (0.8 percent) of acute gastroenteritis; stool specimens from 12 ill guests went ashore at Cozumel to a contracted laboratory, results due Friday 14:00. Overnight cases climb: 52 at 24:00, and at about 05:10 on Friday the 60th passenger case (2.0 percent of 2,980) is recorded, which requires a special report to the CDC Vessel Sanitation Program with a phone call (the plan says within 1 hour), isolation of cases for 48 hours after symptoms stop, closure of self-service stations, a guest letter within 4 hours, and the shoreside crisis call at 08:00. Pressure points: the formal-night gala dinner on Friday with a crew-served buffet, and whether to cancel the show lounge matinee and kids club craft; at 09:00 a passenger posts a video from the Lido deck calling the ship a 'plague ship' with '300 sick' (the true count is 61), and a Houston TV desk calls; the family hotline (800-555-0120) opens; at 14:00 the laboratory confirms norovirus GII, which changes no count or report; the 24-hour report window to the VSP is 19:00 Friday to 07:00 Saturday (counts at 19:00 are 74 passengers and 17 crew; the crew reach 23 cases, 2.0 percent of 1,120, at 22:00 Friday, which needs its own special report); at 08:30 Saturday the passenger count reaches 90 (3.0 percent), an outbreak, requiring a second special report, notice to the flag state, and the shoreside crisis team; Saturday 15:00 a guest in her eighties with a cardiac history (cabin code, not a name) dies in the medical center, a death in the 15 days before arrival that the Master must report to the CDC quarantine station for Houston, a notification to next of kin through Guest Care Director Beatriz Calderón-Fitch, and a media question linking the death to the outbreak (the cause of death is not known to the ship); the 4-hour update is due by 03:00 Sunday if the count changed (it has: 118 passengers, 4.0 percent, and 31 crew); Sunday at 07:00 the ship arrives, the VSP and the Houston quarantine station board; the 3.5-hour turnaround (last guest ashore 10:30, next boarding 14:00, 1,490 cabins, 380 stewards, a full terminal clean at chlorine 1,000 ppm that the stewards cannot finish in time) and the boarding decision for 2,980 booked guests: board on time with an attestation, delay boarding in 2-hour blocks, shorten or cancel, with the first guest message due at least 4 hours before the planned boarding time, travel agents, the terminal operator at the Port of Galveston and the Galveston County Health District to be told. Message consistency is tested across the guest letter, the family hotline script, the media statement and the crew notice: each must state the same signed count and time. The SimCell plays the CDC VSP and the Houston quarantine station, the port, the flag state, the laboratory, guests, a guest's family, reporters, travel agents and the terminal operator.
audience: Director of Public Health and Vessel Sanitation
constraints: Every email address of the line uses the exercise domain halcyonreach.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real cruise line, vessel, airline, agency or newspaper domain; guests appear as cabin codes or role codes, never real names.

Counts are cumulative persons for the voyage with the denominators 2,980 passengers and 1,120 crew (2 percent is 60 and 23, 3 percent is 90 and 34); CDC reports are marked as exercise products and follow the 24 to 36 hour, 4-hour, special report and immediate report rules; guest letters give no medical advice beyond the ship's instructions.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; the CDC, the port, the flag state, the laboratory, guests, families, reporters, travel agents and the terminal operator are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Every channel uses one signed count, reporting clocks run against arrival time, and the decision on whether the next voyage can board on time.
overview.threat: MV Halcyon Dawn sails from Cozumel at 18:00 on Thursday, February 18, 2027. Acute gastroenteritis is already spreading on board: the signed medical log shows 41 passenger cases (1.4 percent of 2,980) and 9 crew cases (0.8 percent of 1,120). Stool specimens from 12 guests are at a contracted lab ashore, with results due Friday at 14:00. No one caused this, but the cases keep rising. Passengers cross 2 percent at about 05:10 Friday (case 60). Crew cross 2 percent at 22:00 Friday (case 23). Passengers reach 3 percent, the outbreak threshold, at 08:30 Saturday (case 90). At 14:00 Friday the lab confirms norovirus GII, which changes no count and no report. A guest in her eighties with a cardiac history dies in the medical center at 15:00 Saturday, and the ship does not know the cause. The Galveston arrival at 07:00 Sunday sets the reporting clocks, and the VSP and the Houston quarantine station board on arrival. The outbreak then runs into the 3.5-hour turnaround for 2,980 booked guests.
overview.operationalImpact:
The facilitator compresses the timeline: the 4-hour exercise covers Thursday 18:00 through the Sunday boarding decision.

**Passengers**
- Ill guests stay in their cabins until 48 hours after symptoms stop.
- Self-service stations close. Players must decide whether to cancel the show lounge matinee and the kids club shared craft, and whether Friday's formal-night gala buffet goes ahead with crew serving.

**Cabin stewards and housekeeping**
- About 40 stewards run dedicated meal-delivery routes to isolated cabins.
- Stewards cannot serve and clean at the same time, so cleaning public areas every 2 hours pulls them from cabin work.

**Medical center**
- The medical center has 20 beds and 3 isolation rooms. It keeps the signed log that every report relies on and manages the death and the cabin code.

**Guest Services and communications**
- At 09:00 Friday a passenger posts a video from the Lido deck claiming "300 sick" when the signed count is 61. A Houston TV desk calls, and the family hotline opens.
- After the death, a reporter asks whether it is linked to the outbreak.
- The guest letter, the hotline script, the media statement and the crew notice must all give the same signed count and time.

**Sunday turnaround (shoreside)**
- Last guest ashore is 10:30 and the next boarding is planned for 14:00, with 1,490 cabins and 380 stewards.
- A full terminal clean at chlorine 1,000 ppm cannot be finished in that window.
- The boarding options are:
 - board on time with an attestation
 - delay in 2-hour blocks
 - shorten or cancel the voyage
- The first guest message must go out at least 4 hours before the planned boarding time. Travel agents, the terminal operator at the Port of Galveston and the Galveston County Health District must also be told.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine (Reporting Clocks)
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to file the 2 percent and 3 percent special reports, the 24-hour and 4-hour pre-arrival reports and the immediate death report to the CDC Quarantine Station for Houston from the signed medical log, each timed against the 07:00 Sunday Galveston arrival and confirmed by the Director of Public Health and Vessel Sanitation before it is sent, as HOPRPG 8 and HR-HSP-02 require.

objectives.name: Containment
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to carry out the HOPRPG 5 stage actions as passengers and crew pass 1, 2 and 3 percent: closing self-service, deciding on the show lounge matinee, the kids club shared craft and the formal-night gala buffet, and splitting about 380 stewards between meal-delivery routes, cabin work and cleaning public areas every 2 hours.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to give one signed count and time in the guest letter, family hotline script, media statement and crew notice, to answer the "300 sick" Lido video within 30 minutes with the count and no denial, and to answer the reporter's question about the death without guessing at the cause and only after the family has been told.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to decide by 10:00 Sunday whether the next voyage boards at 14:00 with an attestation, is delayed in 2-hour blocks, or is shortened or canceled, and to notify the 2,980 booked guests, travel agents, the Galveston terminal operator and the Galveston County Health District as HR-COM-03 7 requires.

roles.name: Master (Captain)
roles.description: Owns the final on-board decisions on cancelling activities, the whole-ship outbreak announcement, the immediate report of the death to the quarantine station, and the reception of the VSP and quarantine station at the gangway on arrival.
standingOrders: Report Now: the death and each threshold report go out when they are due; they do not wait for the family, the lab result or the media.
One Count: you announce or sign off only the count and time in the Chief Medical Officer's signed log.
Containment Over Comfort: the gala buffet and the matinee go ahead only if HOPRPG 5 allows them at the current percentage; guest disappointment does not count as a reason.
Stay Connected: keep the Wi-Fi on; you may ask the shoreside to limit it only for a safety reason, never to control the story.

roles.name: Chief Medical Officer
roles.description: Owns the signed medical log and the case definition, isolation of cases, stool specimens, medical center capacity, care and records for the death, and the count behind every report.
standingOrders: Log Is Truth: a case counts only once it meets the definition and is entered and signed; passengers and crew are counted separately and cumulative totals never go down.
Sign With Time: every count you release carries the time it was signed, so all channels can match it.
Lab Changes Nothing: the norovirus GII result confirms the cause but changes no count and no reporting clock.
Unknown Is an Answer: record the death's cause as unknown until it is known, and do not link it to the outbreak.

roles.name: Hotel Director
roles.description: Manages cleaning and disinfection, food and beverage controls, steward allocation, meal delivery to isolated cabins, guest services and the guest letter on board.
standingOrders: Stewards Are Finite: write down every trade between cabin delivery, 2-hour public-area cleaning and turnaround cleaning; one steward cannot serve and clean at the same time.
Chlorine at Strength: cabins and public areas are disinfected at 1,000 ppm, and records are kept for the VSP at the gangway.
No Self-Service: once passengers or crew reach 2 percent, food is served by crew or not at all, including at the gala.
Letter Matches Log: the guest letter gives the ship's hygiene and isolation instructions and the signed count only, with no medical advice.

roles.name: Vice President, Fleet Operations (shoreside crisis lead)
roles.team: Team D: VP Fleet Operations (shoreside crisis lead)
roles.description: Owns the shoreside crisis team, the 08:00 daily shoreside call, any itinerary change or early return, and the decision on boarding the next voyage in Galveston.
standingOrders: Decide by the Clock: the boarding decision must be made by 10:00 Sunday so that booked guests get notice at least 4 hours before the 14:00 boarding.
Containment Before Turnaround: do not board on time unless the cabin and terminal cleaning, and the attestation behind it, will stand up to the VSP on the dock.
Tell Everyone Together: booked guests, travel agents, the terminal operator, the port and the Galveston County Health District hear the same decision at the same time.
Stand Up at 3 Percent: when passengers reach 90 cases, activate the full crisis team instead of keeping the outbreak a ship-only matter.

roles.name: Director of Public Health and Vessel Sanitation
roles.team: Team E: Director of Public Health and Vessel Sanitation
roles.description: Owns the confirmation of every VSP and quarantine station report, coordination with the CDC, the port health authority and the flag state, and checks of passenger posts against the log.
standingOrders: Confirm Before Send: no report or public count leaves the company until you have matched it to the signed log.
Time to Arrival: count every reporting point back from 07:00 Sunday: 24 to 36 hours before, at least 4 hours before, and the special reports when 2 and 3 percent are reached.
30-Minute Check: check any post claiming a count, a death or a quarantine against the log within 30 minutes and give Communications the facts.
Copy the Partners: send the county and state health departments a copy of each report the same day, and notify the flag state at 3 percent.

roles.name: Vice President, Communications
roles.description: Owns the media statement, the family hotline script, social listening, the crew notice and the messages to the next voyage's guests and travel agents.
standingOrders: Same Count, Every Channel: the statement, hotline, letter and crew notice use the count and time reported to the CDC and nothing else.
Never Deny: answer the "300 sick" video with the statement and the signed count, and correct it with the facts once Public Health has checked it.
Family First: say nothing public about the death until the family has been told, and do not guess at its cause.
Speed With Proof: answer quickly with the count you can confirm rather than waiting for a more complete one.

phases.title: The Count Climbs
phases.goal: Tests whether the medical center and Hotel Director spot a rising case count early, carry out the HOPRPG 5 stage actions at 1 percent, and send the first special report from the signed log when passengers cross 2 percent.
beats: (Thu 18:00) Halcyon Dawn sails from Cozumel. The Chief Medical Officer's signed medical log shows 41 passenger cases (1.4% of 2,980) and 9 crew cases (0.8% of 1,120). Stool specimens from 12 guests are at the contracted Cozumel lab, with results due Fri 14:00. Players must confirm that the 1 percent actions are running under HOPRPG 5: public areas cleaned every 2 hours, written guest notices, masks available and no shared serving utensils.

Noise item: the Purser's office asks whether 2 guests who missed the ship in Cozumel come off the 2,980 denominator posted on the Hotel Director's board. HR-HSP-02 2 fixes the embarkation denominator, so they stay in it.

Strain note: housekeeping reports that the 2-hourly public-area cleaning has pulled cabin stewards off cabin turns and that the 40-steward meal-delivery routes are running late. The 380 stewards cannot serve and clean at the same time.

(Fri 05:10) Passenger case 60 reaches 2 percent. Under HR-HSP-02 5, the Chief Medical Officer must phone the VSP and send the written special report within 1 hour. The Director of Public Health and Vessel Sanitation, Dr. Tobias Wren, confirms it, and copies go to the Galveston County Health District and Texas DSHS.

The HOPRPG 5 2 percent actions start: self-service stations close, all cases are isolated until 48 hours after symptoms stop, stool specimens are collected, and the daily 08:00 shoreside call begins. The Master is asked to rule on the show lounge matinee and the kids club shared craft.

phases.title: Every Channel, One Number
phases.goal: Tests whether one signed count and time reach every channel under public pressure, whether a confirmed lab result is kept from changing counts or reports, and whether the 24-hour report and the crew and 3 percent special reports go out on time.
beats: (Fri 09:00) A passenger posts a Lido deck video claiming "300 sick" while the signed count is 61. A Houston TV desk calls, and the family hotline opens. The VP Communications has 30 minutes to answer with the signed count and time and no denial, under HR-COM-03 6.

(Fri 14:00) The Cozumel lab confirms norovirus GII. Red herring: a SimCell inject from a crew department head blames the Cozumel tender food and pushes to re-categorize cases. Players must hold that the result changes no count and no report and goes in the report content only as a lab result.
The formal-night gala buffet decision: it either goes ahead with crew serving or is cancelled. Steward allocation is rebalanced between meal routes, cabin work and public-area cleaning.

(Fri 19:00 to Sat 07:00) The 24-hour report window to the VSP opens for the 07:00 Sunday Galveston arrival. The report gives cumulative passenger and crew cases, signed by the Chief Medical Officer, countersigned by the Master and confirmed by Dr. Tobias Wren.

(Fri 22:00) Crew case 23 reaches the crew 2 percent special report. (Sat 08:30) Passenger case 90 reaches 3 percent, which triggers the second special report, the shoreside crisis team under Colleen Abernathy-Reyes, the guest letter, a whole-ship outbreak announcement and Bahamas Maritime Authority notification (HR-HSP-02 6). The guest letter, hotline script, media statement and crew notice must all match the log.

phases.title: Death and the Boarding Call
phases.goal: Tests the immediate death report, telling the family first, and the single decision point: by 10:00 Sunday, whether the next voyage boards at 14:00 with an attestation, is delayed in 2-hour blocks, or is shortened or cancelled.
beats: (Sat 15:00) Guest A, in her eighties with a cardiac history and staying in a cabin coded for the exercise, dies in the medical center, and the cause is unknown. The Master must make the immediate report to the CDC Quarantine Station for Houston by phone and electronic message (HR-HSP-02 5). The report does not wait for the family. Guest Care Director Beatriz Calderón-Fitch arranges for the family to be told before any public statement.

(Sat 17:00) A Galveston reporter asks whether the death is linked to the outbreak. The VP Communications must not guess at the cause and must not answer until the family has been told. The answer uses the same signed count and time.

(Sun 03:00) The 4-hour update is due because the count changed after the 24-hour report. Cumulative counts must not go down. The terminal operator and the Port of Galveston are told the expected arrival.

(Sun 07:00) Arrival in Galveston. The VSP and the Houston quarantine station board, and the Master and the Environmental Officer meet them at the gangway with the plan, the log, cleaning records and food and water records. The VSP advises delaying boarding and a terminal clean.

DECISION POINT (Sun 10:00): The Master, Dr. Tobias Wren and VP Fleet Operations Colleen Abernathy-Reyes weigh the HOPRPG 7 options against the 72-hour trend, onsets in the last 48 hours, cabin-cleaning status and VSP advice. Boarding on time with an attestation risks spreading the outbreak to the next voyage. A delay, shortened voyage or cancellation strands 2,980 booked guests who have been told check-in opens at 13:00. The first guest message is due by 10:00 under the 4-hour rule.

phases.title: Turnaround Under Pressure
phases.goal: Tests whether the chosen boarding option is carried out with verified cleaning and complete notifications: booked guests, travel agents, the terminal operator and the Galveston County Health District, as HR-COM-03 7 requires.
beats: (Sun 10:30) The last guest is ashore. Port Operations Manager Hector Salazar sets the cleaning order with the terminal operator: cabins first (1,490 cabins, 380 stewards), then public areas, with the terminal last. Provisioning from 12 trucks and the crew changeover compete for the same window.

Hurdle: the shipboard chlorine mixing station fails a 1,000 ppm concentration check partway through the clean, and the terminal operator says a full terminal clean cannot be finished before 14:00. Players must decide whether to hold boarding for another 2-hour block.
Verification: the VSP walks the cleaned areas and reviews cleaning records before the attestation is signed. The Master and Dr. Tobias Wren must not attest to an area that has not been checked.

Notifications go out with one signed count and time: the hold or boarding message to 2,980 booked guests, plus the travel agencies, the national travel association, the terminal operator, the Galveston County Health District, Texas DSHS and the local TV desks. The family hotline script is updated after the death.
(Sun ~13:30) The facilitator collects after-action notes on the reporting clocks, consistency across channels and the boarding decision, then calls ENDEX.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The objective is about filing the VSP and quarantine station reports that HR-HSP-02 5 requires: the 2 and 3 percent special reports, the 24-hour report, the 4-hour update and the immediate death report. Each one comes from the signed medical log and is timed against the 07:00 Sunday Galveston arrival.

Each report has to be signed, countersigned and confirmed by the Director of Public Health and Vessel Sanitation. Copies go to the county and state health departments, the flag state and the terminal, as HR-HSP-02 5 and 6 require. This keeps the ship, shoreside and the authorities on one set of numbers and times.
At each HOPRPG 5 stage the ship must isolate cases, extending isolation to 48 hours after symptoms stop at 2 percent, and disinfect cabins at 1,000 ppm.

The HOPRPG 5 stage actions are split between the Hotel Director, the Master and shoreside. Players must close self-service, rule on the matinee, the kids club craft and the gala buffet, divide the stewards between duties, and stand up the shoreside crisis team at 3 percent.

The guest letter, hotline script, media statement and crew notice must all carry one signed count and time, as HR-HSP-02 8 requires. The holding statement must follow the HR-COM-03 5 deadline, and reporters' questions about the death must be answered without guessing at the cause.

Under HOPRPG 7, the Master, the Public Health director and VP Fleet Operations decide together on boarding: on time with an attestation, delayed in 2-hour blocks, shortened or canceled. The decision weighs the case trend, the cleaning status and the advice from the VSP.

Under HOPRPG 7, any delay or change has to be announced to the 2,980 booked guests, travel partners and the terminal operator as soon as it is decided, with the first guest message no later than 4 hours before the planned boarding time.

hotwash.methodDescription: 3-Up, 3-Down: ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during the exercise, so everyone sees both strengths and gaps before memories fade. Go around the room team by team (bridge, medical, hotel/F&B, communications, shoreside) and write each Up and Down on the whiteboard in that team's own words. Don't debate them until every team has spoken.

questions.text: Passengers crossed 2 percent at about 05:10 Friday (case 60), crew crossed it at 22:00 Friday, and passengers hit 3 percent at 08:30 Saturday. Policy in HR-HSP-02 5 is a phone call plus a written special report within 1 hour of the count that reached the threshold. When did you actually see each crossing in the signed medical log, and when did each special report leave with the Director of Public Health's confirmation? You had the 24:00 log showing 52 cases in I-02. What would have let you see the 05:10 crossing coming instead of finding it afterwards?

At 15:00 Saturday a guest in her eighties with a cardiac history died in the medical center, and you did not know the cause. Under HR-HSP-02 5, the Master reports any death in the 15 days before arrival to the Houston quarantine station right away. Did you file it right away or wait for a cause? Who was told first: the family, the CDC, or the reporter? When the press asked, did anyone link the death to norovirus or rule it out before there was any evidence?

At 02:14 Friday the Roll Call post (I-02b) claimed 'over 100 locked in their cabins' and a cover-up, and a travel agent with 22 clients on the next sailing was following it. Later the '300 sick' Lido video gave you 30 minutes to respond. Did the guest letter, family hotline script, media statement and crew notice all quote the same signed count and time? Did any of them deny the outbreak or soften it? What did you tell the public before the 14:00 Friday lab result, and did it change once norovirus was confirmed?

Over the 23:50 field report (I-02) and the 11:30 gala staffing memo (I-06), the hotel team kept asking the same thing: 380 stewards can't cover isolation trays, the 2-hour public-area cycle, cabin turns and a 64-server gala all at once. Gowns were down to 31 percent. Did you treat those messages as evidence that containment was failing, or as a staffing ticket to clear? What did you decide for the self-service buffet, the kids club craft, the matinee and the gala, and who owned the decision on what to drop?

At 08:50 Sunday (I-14) you had a full clean ending around 18:30, a 14:00 boarding that meant attesting on about 45 percent of cabins cleaned, and a terminal operator who needed an answer by 09:45, earlier than your 10:00 call. Which option did you pick: board with an attestation, delay in 2-hour blocks, shorten or cancel? Did the 2,980 booked guests, 318 agents, the terminal and the Galveston County Health District hear it from you before the news? Looking back, which input from Friday or Saturday would have let you make this call a day earlier?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Duty manager, Gulf Terminal Services (terminal operator at the Port of Galveston). Also speaks for the Port of Galveston port police and the travel agencies that depend on the terminal, such as the Coastline Getaways group desk

hardQuestions: I've got 14 buses and 2 security lanes booked from 13:00 and 2,980 people told 13:00. Is that decision in writing, and who signed it? I'm not re-laning a terminal on a phone call.
The port police wanted your berth-time update by 05:00. Did that go to them, or am I the first one hearing it?
Who signs off my check-in hall as clean? Your Environmental Officer or my crew? My people can't finish before about 15:30, so are you holding another two hours or not? I need to know by 12:20.
The 140-person group agent is on my other line. She says your text, your website and Gulf 8 all give different numbers. Which number and which time do I tell her?
concessions: Will re-lane and stage buses if a written decision with a set new boarding time (in 2-hour blocks) reaches the terminal by 09:45 (or 12:20 for an extension).
Will hold terminal cleaning crews past 14:00 and accept the Environmental Officer's sign-off as the release point once the line confirms it in writing.
Will pass the line's single signed count and new time to waiting guests and agency reps at the curb, but only if the line gives one written message the terminal can read out.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Duty officer, then lead inspector, CDC Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP)

hardQuestions: Is that number from your signed log? What time was it signed? Give me passengers and crew separately, cumulative since embarkation 14 February. I'll want the written special report after this call.
Your galley chef wants shore-food cases in a separate column. Do they meet the case definition? If yes, they're cases. Did you just make your crew count go down?
Your 4-hour update has 44 passengers in the field marked 'cumulative'. Your 24-hour report said 74. Which is it?
Your disinfection record has an unsigned 16:00 Lido round on Thursday and '4-hourly' entries for Decks 5 to 11 on Saturday night. Explain that before you ask me about boarding.
concessions: Will accept the phone notification as on time if the written special report, signed by the CMO and countersigned by the Master, follows promptly, and will agree a time for daily updates.
Will review a staged embarkation plan, but only for areas with signed 1,000 ppm records and the Environmental Officer's walk-through. Will not endorse the blanket attestation draft.

Will start galley and Lido sampling at once and share timing so cleaning can be planned around it, if the Master and Environmental Officer have the plan, log, cleaning records and food and water records at the gangway.

hardQuestions: Time of death, and what time did you call me? The report is immediate, by phone and electronic message. Has the message gone, or only this call?
Is she an AGE case? Is her cabin companion a case, and since when? Don't tell me the cause unless your doctor knows it.
Is the cabin sealed and the medical record kept intact for me and for the county medical examiner, who is arriving at 08:30?
What count are you reporting with this, and when was it signed?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. The aim is to test plans, reporting clocks and decisions, not to grade the Master, the Chief Medical Officer or any other player.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the case counts, lab results and timings in each module and inject as written, even where real voyages might differ.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including HOPRPG, HR-HSP-02 and HR-ORG-04. Where a plan is silent or unclear, players say so and describe what they would actually do.
Every count used in discussion comes from the most recent signed medical log entry, with the time it was signed. Percentages use the persons on board at embarkation: 2,980 passengers and 1,120 crew.
Players have the knowledge and authority of their real positions. Decisions made in one module carry forward as the facilitator's time-jump cards describe.
artificialities: Time is compressed and jumps between modules. Four hours of play cover the period from Thursday 18:00 to about 13:30 Sunday ship time. Each time-jump card states what has changed and assumes that earlier decisions are in force.

The Simulation Cell (SimCell) plays everyone outside the room. This includes the CDC Vessel Sanitation Program, the CDC Quarantine Station for Houston, the Galveston County Health District, Texas DSHS, the Bahamas Maritime Authority, Gulf Terminal Services, the Port of Galveston, the Cozumel laboratory, travel agencies, the Roatán excursion operator, reporters, guests, next of kin and onboard department heads not in the room.

Systems are named as in the plans but are not touched. The medical log, the VSP reporting channel, the family hotline, the chlorine mixing station and the guest-messaging tools are represented only by printed exercise products.

Injects are delivered on paper or on screen: phone slips, emails, social media posts, log entries and face-to-face scripts. Players answer them verbally or in writing and do not send any real message.
Cleaning, staffing and laundry capacities are planning figures used for discussion. No crew, stewards or terminal staff are moved during the exercise.

It is 14:45 Central ship time on Saturday, February 20, the final sea day. The ship is about 330 nautical miles south of Galveston. At 07:00 tomorrow the ship arrives at a terminal where 2,980 guests for the next voyage have been told check-in opens at 13:00, about 3.5 hours after the last guest is due ashore. For this module, the next hour runs from Saturday afternoon through Sunday morning.

You have 1,490 cabins, 380 stewards, one chlorine mixing station and 14 tons a day of laundry capacity. Nothing has been verified clean yet.
